issues.failure_explanation: Taking the ratio of the displayed Racah summands gives -[z+2]_q times \prod_y[b_y-z]_q divided by \prod_i[z+1-a_i]_q. The source instead places the i-factors in the numerator, the y-factors in the denominator, and shifts the latter to b_y-(z+1). Thus its recurrence does not reproduce the series.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the ratio by the correctly derived consecutive-term ratio and propagate that correction through compilation and projection.
issues.overall_effect: The compiled ratio sequence and all evaluations based on it need not equal the stated quantum 6j-symbol; the construction-based proof of deformation as evaluation consequently fails for this example.
issues.title: The stated consecutive-term ratio for the quantum 6j sum is inverted
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, uniquely determined recurrence correction and does not require changing the method or its intended guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The first term reflects the intrinsic summation error governed strictly by the condition number of the amplitude

issues.failure_explanation: The exponent-vector cancellations reduce common multiplicative factors within each summand. They do not perform exact additive cancellation between distinct alternating summands, which is precisely what the defined condition number kappa measures. The paper's later error discussion itself retains kappa as an intrinsic limitation.

failure_location.quote: In particular, the large intermediate cancellations to resolve the condition number $\kappa$ in Section~\ref{subsec:cancellation} are no longer realized numerically, but are instead resolved exactly at the algebraic level.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to exact multiplicative cancellation within individual terms and explicitly state that additive cancellation represented by kappa remains numerical.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the representation algebraically resolves condition-number-driven cancellation is false; only representation-induced within-term inflation can be reduced, while the alternating sum remains ill-conditioned.
issues.title: The DCR is claimed to resolve cancellation measured by the sum condition number
issues.why_classification: The method remains useful, but repair withdraws a substantive stability explanation and narrows the advertised preconditioning effect.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State $\mathcal{R}_z \gets$ compute cyclotomic factorization of the ratio via Eq.~\eqref{eq:ratio_Rz}
For the quantum $6j$-symbol, one obtains the explicit ratio

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm accepts an arbitrary q-hypergeometric series, but its only instruction for constructing updates invokes Eq. eq:ratio_Rz, which is explicitly derived only for the quantum 6j-symbol and depends on its a_i and b_y data. No step derives the ratio from a generic input series, so the procedure is not defined on its stated input class.

failure_location.quote: \Require A $q$-hypergeometric series $S(q)$ with external parameters (e.g. spins $j$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the algorithm's input contract to the quantum 6j-symbol or add a concrete procedure that derives and factors the consecutive-term ratio from the generic affine factorial data.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised compilation algorithm does not establish a DCR constructor for general finite q-hypergeometric series.
issues.title: The generic compilation algorithm hardcodes a quantum 6j-specific ratio
issues.why_classification: A generic repair requires a nontrivial input representation and ratio-construction step; restricting the contract would materially narrow, though not destroy, the framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The entire square root is resolved at the exponent level, without field extension

issues.failure_explanation: An arbitrary field need not contain a square root of Pi_T(M_rad), so the returned expression need not lie in T. Even over C, a square-root branch must be specified to make the projection unambiguous. Integer exponent bookkeeping isolates the radical but does not remove the required algebraic extension or branch choice at evaluation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require a target field containing a specified square root of the projected radicand, or return an element of an explicitly constructed quadratic extension with a fixed root convention.
issues.overall_effect: The universal target-field contract, the exact-projection claim, and the assertion that no field extension is required are unreliable for amplitudes with nontrivial radical prefactors.
issues.title: Projection into an arbitrary target field is not closed under the required square root
issues.why_classification: The exponent representation survives, but the projection API and universal-field guarantee require a substantive domain or codomain change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Any cyclotomic monomial containing a factor $\Phi_h(q^2)$ with positive exponent vanishes identically, while a negative exponent produces a pole.

issues.failure_explanation: A projected ratio may vanish because it has positive Phi_h valuation, while a later ratio may have negative Phi_h valuation. The formal cumulative product can then have a finite or nonzero specialization after cancellation even though evaluating ratios sequentially produces 0 followed by a pole. Nothing in the algorithm establishes that, once a ratio vanishes, every later formal term has positive net valuation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Track cumulative cyclotomic valuations symbolically and terminate only after proving that every remaining term vanishes, or remove the early-termination step.
issues.overall_effect: At roots of unity the algorithm can omit later nonzero or removable-singularity terms and return an incorrect amplitude.
issues.title: A zero update ratio does not justify terminating all later summands
issues.why_classification: Removing the optimization is easy, but preserving it requires a genuine monotonicity or support argument absent from the source; the core projection method otherwise remains intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: while a negative exponent produces a pole.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition quantifies over all integer exponent vectors. If e_h<0, specialization requires inversion of Phi_h(q^2)=0, so Pi_q(M) is not an element of the target field and the asserted equality-to-zero biconditional is not defined. Moreover, this elementary vanishing criterion alone does not characterize admissibility when normalized expressions may have poles or cancellations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the proposition to monomials whose specialization is defined, handle negative and canceling valuations before projection, and weaken the claimed connection to admissibility unless an equivalence for complete amplitudes is proved.
issues.overall_effect: The formal proposition and the broader interpretation of root-of-unity admissibility as simple positive support are not valid on the stated domain.
issues.title: The root-of-unity admissibility proposition applies projection where a generator is noninvertible
issues.why_classification: The elementary zero criterion is recoverable, but the unrestricted statement and its advertised admissibility interpretation require more than a cosmetic domain edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Precomputation of cyclotomic data up to $D_{\max}$ contributes $\mathcal{O}(D_{\max})$.
This produces a dense table in $\mathcal{O}(D \log D)$ time
\mathcal{O}\!\left( D_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} + Z \cdot K \cdot S_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} \right)

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem charges only O(D_max) for precomputing cyclotomic data, whereas the paper's own recursive construction states O(D log D). Enumerating and processing proper divisors over all indices likewise has total divisor-incidence cost of that order. The same omitted factor appears in the evaluation proposition's precomputation term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the source's O(D_max log D_max) precomputation bound in both results and consistently account for divisor enumeration and any exponentiation costs.
issues.overall_effect: The stated construction and evaluation bounds are understated, and the claimed effective linearity is not established in the displayed form.
issues.title: The complexity bounds omit the stated divisor-table precomputation cost
issues.why_classification: The correction changes the formal asymptotic bounds but only by contained logarithmic factors and does not require replacing the architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The quantity $\gamma_{\text{rep}}$ precisely isolates the contribution of the representation choice to the total numerical error.

issues.failure_explanation: No rounding analysis connects the sum of logarithmic numerator and denominator magnitudes to the asserted forward-error term. The statistic is not invariant under replacing N_z,D_z by cN_z,cD_z, which leaves T_z unchanged but shifts gamma_rep by 2 log10|c|; it can also be negative. Thus it cannot by itself be an amplification factor in a general error bound, and subtraction of logarithms does not incur error proportional merely to the magnitudes represented by those logarithms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a rounding-error analysis for the actual algorithms using a well-defined, scale-invariant representation condition measure, or withdraw Eq. eq:forwd_error and present the stability comparison as empirical only.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical numerical-stability bound, the interpretation of gamma_rep, and claims that the empirical dynamic-range table validates that bound are unsupported.
issues.title: The proposed floating-point error law has no valid dependence on the dynamic-range statistic
issues.why_classification: A valid replacement requires a nontrivial contained error analysis or abandonment of the paper's theoretical stability model, although the empirical comparisons can remain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which requires a coherent summation over all admissible spin colorings $\{j\}$:

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed state sum contains only tetrahedral 6j factors and a global normalization. A Turaev-Viro state sum also requires local quantum-dimension weights for the colored edges; these depend on the coloring and cannot be absorbed into the constant A^{-|V|}. Thus the displayed expression is not the claimed partition function.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the product of the appropriate quantum-dimension edge weights and include their projection and aggregation costs in the discussion.
issues.overall_effect: The macroscopic application is analyzed using an incomplete state-sum amplitude, so the displayed formula does not define the stated invariant.
issues.title: The displayed Turaev-Viro partition function omits edge weights
issues.why_classification: The omitted factors are standard local multiplicative weights that fit directly into the same representation and do not require new proof architecture.
